source.purpose: Reference database for PSLE Science answering, scientific key words, causal explanation chains, comparison wording and topic coverage. This source informs application marking and training-model generation but does not overwrite the existing memorisation bank unless explicitly approved.

answering_principles.rule: For gaseous-exchange questions, state the substance, the exchange surface/organ and the direction of movement. Link the exchanged gas to the body process or transport outcome when the question asks why.
examples: oxygen enters the blood and is transported to body parts
carbon dioxide is transported from body parts to the gaseous-exchange organ for removal

answering_principles.rule: For exercise questions, build the complete chain: muscles/body need more energy -> respiration increases -> more oxygen and digested food are needed -> breathing/heart rate increases -> more oxygen/digested food is delivered and carbon dioxide/waste is removed faster.

For comparisons, explicitly state both sides. Similarity format: 'Both A and B ...'. Difference format: 'A ..., while B ...'. If the diagram asks for direction/richness of blood, quote the diagram labels before explaining.
When asked how body systems work together, explain each system's contribution and then the transport/link between them. Do not merely name the systems.
patterns: digestive system breaks food into simple substances and absorbs them into blood -> circulatory system transports digested food
respiratory system exchanges gases -> circulatory system transports oxygen to body parts and carbon dioxide away

answering_principles.rule: For stem-cut/ring-removal questions, identify which transport tubes are damaged, state what substance can no longer reach which part, then state the resulting effect on the plant.

For photosynthesis explanations, protect the conditions and products: light energy, chlorophyll, water and carbon dioxide are linked to production of sugar/food and oxygen. If the question is about plant survival/growth, link food production to energy/life processes after respiration.

For population-change questions, use EFP: Event -> Food relationship -> Population change. State the event first, then how food/predator/prey availability changes, then the direction of the population change.
In food chains/webs, arrows show the direction of energy transfer from the organism being eaten to the organism that eats it. Use the arrow direction before deciding predator/prey relationships.

When naming the process carried out by decomposers, use 'decomposition' rather than 'decomposing'. Explain that decomposers break down dead organisms/waste into simpler substances such as mineral salts, returning nutrients to the environment.

key_ideas: Air contains mainly nitrogen and oxygen, with smaller amounts of carbon dioxide and water vapour.
Fish take in dissolved oxygen in water through the mouth and gills; oxygen enters the blood and is transported to body parts.
Carbon dioxide from the body is transported to the gills and removed into the surrounding water.
Tiny openings/stomata allow gaseous exchange in plants.
Smaller or fewer exposed openings can reduce water loss through evaporation.
Photosynthesis takes place during daytime when light is available; chlorophyll, water and carbon dioxide are needed, and oxygen and food are produced.
answering_notes: If the body is less active, less energy is needed, so respiration is slower and less carbon dioxide is produced.
For function questions on stomata, name gaseous exchange and, where relevant, water-vapour loss.

key_ideas: The circulatory system consists of the heart, blood vessels and blood.
The heart pumps blood around the body.
Blood transports oxygen and digested food to body parts and carries carbon dioxide and waste materials away for removal.

In humans, blood flows in two circular pathways and passes through the heart twice; the photographed book contrasts this with fish circulation, where blood flows in one circular pathway and passes through the heart once.
Humans use lungs for gaseous exchange; fish use gills.
Both human and fish circulatory systems have blood vessels that carry blood throughout the body.

chain: more oxygen and digested food are needed
oxygen/digested food are transported faster and carbon dioxide/waste removed faster

model_reasoning_patterns.rule: Use the labelled direction and whether blood is richer in oxygen/carbon dioxide before explaining where gaseous exchange occurred.

key_ideas: Digestive system: digestion begins in the mouth, food is broken into smaller/simple substances, digestion is completed in the small intestine, and digested food is absorbed into the blood.
Water from undigested food is absorbed in the large intestine; waste leaves through the anus.
Respiratory system enables gaseous exchange with the surroundings.
Circulatory system transports substances around the body.
Muscular system works with the skeletal system to allow movement.
Skeletal system supports the body, gives shape and protects important organs.

system_link_chains.chain: food is broken down into simple substances -> digested food is absorbed into blood -> circulatory system transports it to body parts
oxygen is taken in/exchanged at lungs -> oxygen enters blood -> circulatory system transports it to body parts; carbon dioxide is carried back for removal

key_ideas: Roots absorb water and mineral salts.
Water-carrying tubes transport water and mineral salts from roots to other parts of the plant.
Food-carrying tubes transport food made in the leaves to other parts of the plant.
During photosynthesis, carbon dioxide enters leaves and oxygen leaves through stomata.
During respiration, oxygen enters and carbon dioxide leaves through stomata.

damage_examples.situation: cut around stem removing food-carrying tubes below the cut
damage_examples.effect: food made by leaves cannot be transported to parts below the cut; food may accumulate above the cut, causing swelling

damage_examples.situation: deep cut damaging both water- and food-carrying tubes
damage_examples.effect: food cannot be transported to all parts and water/mineral salts from roots cannot be transported to all parts; over time the plant may die

key_ideas: The Sun is the main source of energy for organisms; plants trap light energy directly during photosynthesis and animals obtain energy indirectly through food.
Photosynthesis occurs in plants in the presence of light.
Water and carbon dioxide, with light and chlorophyll, are used to make food/sugar and oxygen.
Excess sugar may be stored as starch.
Respiration occurs in living cells, releases energy from food and occurs in plants and animals.
Respiration uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide and water according to the book's summary.
topics.comparison_rule: When comparing photosynthesis and respiration, state both processes explicitly and compare timing, gases taken in/given out and where they occur.

key_ideas: A population is a group of organisms of the same kind living together and reproducing in a particular place, including young and adults.
A habitat is the place where an organism lives.
A community is made of different populations living together in the same habitat.
Population size increases through reproduction or movement into an area and decreases through death or movement out of an area.
Living factors include food and other organisms; non-living factors include soil, temperature, air, light and water.
Organisms compete for limited resources such as food, water, light and space.
Only plants can trap light energy directly from the Sun during photosynthesis.
Food chains show feeding relationships and energy transfer; they begin with a producer.
Food webs are formed from interconnected food chains.
A change in one population can affect other populations through feeding relationships.

ecology_reasoning_patterns.chain: fewer predators -> fewer prey eaten -> prey population may increase
less food available -> more competition / less food for predator -> predator population may decrease
less light -> less photosynthesis -> less food made -> insufficient food for life processes -> plant may die
dead organisms/waste -> decomposers carry out decomposition -> simpler substances/mineral salts returned to environment -> nutrients can be used by plants

population_answer_framework.name: EFP
steps: F — Food relationship: explain how the change affects food/predator/prey availability
P — Population change: state which population increases/decreases and why

integration_policy.memorisation_bank: Do not replace the existing 89 memorised sentences automatically.
integration_policy.training_models: Use these notes to make application models more complete, especially for causal chains, comparison questions, system-link questions and population-change questions.
integration_policy.ai_marker: Use these source-derived key words and causal links as supporting evidence when deciding whether required D/E, S/R and L/R components are complete; do not require extra science that the question does not ask for.
